body.statement:
Suppose \(\alpha\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)\), set \(\beta=\alpha/L\), and let \(\eta>0\) be the predeclared rational tolerance.  Then
\[
\Pr\{\Delta_\ell\in I_\ell\text{ for every }1\le\ell\le L\}\ge1-\alpha
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Pr\{\overline\Delta\in\overline I\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
There exists a finite constant \(C_\alpha\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed role-share bounds, such that
\[
\mathbb E\{\operatorname{diam}(\overline I)\}
\le C_\alpha\left\{\frac{\max(1,\sqrt{n\rho})}{n}+\eta\right\}.
\]
body.justification: The fixed fifteen-pair target needs simultaneous rather than pointwise validity before interval averaging.
body.gap: The published block bootstrap aggregates interior influence functions and does not guarantee finite-sample coverage at zero counts.
body.consumer: The Buenos Aires-style fifteen-comparison DTT aggregate receives one causal-scale interval with a transparent multiplicity correction.
body.proof_tex:
The identification proposition gives \(\Delta_\ell=G(r_{\ell1},\ldots,r_{\ell4})\).  Because \(r_{\ell j}=\rho c_{\ell j}\), the coefficient and rarity bounds imply \(r_\ell\in\mathcal P_0\).  When \(\eta\le1/n\), the rational outer-interval theorem, applied pairwise with \(\beta=\alpha/L\), gives
\[
\Pr(\Delta_\ell\notin I_\ell)\le\frac{\alpha}{L}.
\]
When \(\eta>1/n\), the same conclusion follows directly from equations (1)--(6) of that theorem's proof: the construction and coverage argument use only \(\eta>0\), and its diameter proof gives the same bound with the now larger additive term \(\eta\).  Thus the marginal guarantee and diameter order hold for every positive rational \(\eta\).
No cross-pair independence is needed for the union bound, which yields
\[
\Pr\{\Delta_\ell\in I_\ell\text{ for every }\ell\}
\ge1-\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac\alpha L=1-\alpha.
\]
On this simultaneous event, if \(I_\ell=[L_\ell,U_\ell]\), then
\[
L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^LL_\ell
\le L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Delta_\ell
\le L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^LU_\ell,
\]
so \(\overline\Delta\in\overline I\).  Finally,
\[
\operatorname{diam}(\overline I)
=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\operatorname{diam}(I_\ell).
\]
Taking expectations and applying the pairwise diameter bound with the fixed value \(\beta=\alpha/L\) proves the asserted order after absorbing the fixed number \(L=15\) into \(C_\alpha\).
